node.label: Nancy Christie
node.date_label: A Full-Orbed Christianity, with Michael Gauvreau (1996) · Engendering the State (2000) · Christian Churches and Their Peoples, with Michael Gauvreau (2010)
node.description: A Canadian historian of family, welfare and religion whose work asks how liberal authority was made through everyday institutions. In her 2009 contribution to the liberal-order debate, Christie credits Ian McKay’s framework with connecting cultural and social research while disputing its periodization, its emphasis on the state and its property-based account of individualism. Drawing on Bruce Curtis’s distinction between liberalism and governmentality, she asks for a more precise account of power. She proposes treating churches, voluntary associations and households as places where liberal values were made and contested, so that women’s participation, not only their exclusion, becomes part of the explanation. Engendering the State (2000) and her books with Michael Gauvreau on Protestant churches and social welfare place these institutions at the centre of Canadian social history.
